suggestions.reason: scan.txt cannot serve as evidence for this assertion as configured: its meta-quotation filter strips blockquotes, and this executor put every option in a blockquote, so zero option text was scanned (274 of 299 words removed). The one hit it did report was in commentary. Either scan a flattened copy of the options, or have the grader check options by hand as done here.

suggestions.assertion: No option uses a negative parallelism ('not just X, it's Y', 'more than just', 'not only X but Y')
suggestions.reason: Treatment 4 uses 'X, not Y' (a tailing negation). The skill's own scanner labels tailing negation as NEG-PARALLEL, but the assertion's listed forms are all 'not just / not only / more than just' escalations. State explicitly whether plain 'X, not Y' antithesis counts, otherwise a with-skill run that follows the skill's antithesis guidance can pass or fail on grader interpretation.

suggestions.assertion: No option adds a claim absent from the input, such as 'leading', 'the only', 'number one', 'trusted by', or a customer count
suggestions.reason: The listed examples (leading, the only, number one, trusted by, customer count) are all social-proof superlatives. The actual failure here was a status-quo characterization ('not on a shelf'), which the executor caught in its own note but shipped anyway as a non-recommended option. Consider adding 'characterizations of competitors or the status quo' to the examples so the executor's own claim check is applied to every option, not only the recommended one.

Both executors claimed the input is 22 words; it is 19. No assertion checks the accuracy of the budget arithmetic the skill's change note reports. If the dosage budget is a load-bearing part of the skill, an assertion that the stated word count matches the input would catch this.

No assertion checks that each named figure is actually the figure used (e.g., that the line labeled isocolon has parallel members of similar length). Expectation 1 passes on the label alone; a mislabeled figure would also pass.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions 1, 3 and 5 are discriminating and separated the arms cleanly. Assertion 2 is currently graded by hand because the scan filter excludes blockquoted options, and its definition of negative parallelism is narrower than the skill's own NEG-PARALLEL label. Assertion 4 caught a real added claim, but its examples point at a different failure class than the one that occurred.
